newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cotton imports little changed in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German cotton imports little changed in 1996.

text.p: German cotton imports in 1996 were up by 0.4 percent from 1995 at 142,497 tonnes (654,481 bales), the Bremen Cotton Exchange said in a report on Monday.
Sales values dropped by 4.6 percent over 1995 to 383 million marks.
The average price per kilo of 2.69 marks compared with 2.83 in 1995, 2.52 marks in the early 1990s, 3.49 marks in the 1980s and 2.99 marks in the 1970s.
Asian countries accounted for 58 percent of the import total (53 percent in 1995).
Uzbekistan alone accounted for 49 percent, with 69,781 tonnes, followed by Greece with 16,927 tonnes, Turkmenistan with 8,473 tonnes, Chad with 8,384 tonnes and the United States with 5,485.
Domestic textile industries remained under pressure from cheap finished products imports, the Exchange said.
But export demand picked up and certain European Union restrictions on third country imports also helped relieve the internal supply side.
Spinners in 1996 produced 125,540 tonnes of cotton yarn, 5.5 percent less than in 1995.
Operating margins were depressed by overcapacity.
